title: Outgrown
notes: Narration as now written: 'In pounds, it never went away. It ended bigger.' and 'registered unemployment'. CHART-10B-A shows why: the pounds line dips in 1948, 1951 and 1969, so it did not 'keep rising'; it ends at £39bn.

Charts are full-frame on V2. A and B are entered part-way (src_in 0.8 and 2.5, not 0) so each finishes drawing exactly as its line ends; with the real voice, lengthen them back toward src_in 0. C plays whole (6.0 s) under 'For twenty-seven years running…'.

Verb card VERB-1946-1973-PLANT: the storyboard says 'held over the falling line'. Cards are opaque, so the cut returns to CHART-10B-C's last frame (the red line at 48%) on 'Britain did not shrink to fit its debt' and the verb card follows it on 'It outgrew it'. In Premiere it can be built as the card's type over the chart. The plan put the card before London Airport; the airport's control tower now comes first.

'Housed, treated, and in work' departs from the plan (Festival crowds / new school / foundry): housed = Your Very Good Health's new house with a pram at the door (colour); treated = Charley Junior's School Days' nurse holding a baby (colour); in work = Wonder Jet's rolling mill, hot steel strip snaking across the floor (B/W). Festival in London is not used: its crowds do not say housed, treated or in work.

The Pop Goes the Weasel bench: two men with a paper under 'Not by magic. Budgets were tight.'; the man in overalls reading, then his close-up, under the lenders-and-savers line ('Quietly.' lands on his face).
DIP to black into Movement 4 at the end of 10b-14.
